feature: A 24 unit artboard rules itself into units
summary: With the Grid on, an icon frame or icon picture shows one quiet line on every unit, counted from its corner, so you can see where a point will land. Moving, resizing or nudging something inside it lands on those lines.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/a-24-unit-artboard-rules-itself-walk.json.

evaluate: Can you count units on the artboard without the lines competing with the keylines?
Is it right that the units appear only with the Grid on, as the mock's step 1 has it, rather than on every icon frame?
Does the jump at 600%, where the units give way to the canvas grid below it, feel natural as you zoom?
Is a line every unit still quiet enough at 600%, where they are six points apart?
rough: Decided against icon-draw-wt.html: the units show only with the Grid on, because the mock's artboard stays plain until step 1 turns the grid on. Show Grid in the View menu is that step, your call on 2026-10-20.

Measured on the real window at 3200%: 23 lines each way, every one 64 pixels from the next. Unit lines stand 21 levels off a white artboard and 16 off a near black one, against 124 and 154 for a keyline.
The mock marks the live area and the square with closed dashed outlines; the app keeps its wash and its hairlines that run off the edges, per UX-PATTERNS §D16.
The mock's Snap to step lights a dot on every crossing. The app draws none yet, folded into icon-snapping-reaches-what-the-icon-mock-draws.
Under six points a unit nothing is ruled, so a big icon at fit zoom, such as a 1024 app icon, still shows the canvas grid running across it.
A grid set to Columns only still rules both ways on an artboard, because the units are the frame's own and whole units pull both ways.
